You belong to one Tessl organization, so it will not ask you to pick one. `carnival` is only a suggestion. Any name is fine. When it finishes, tell me the name and I will link `tjlovescode/tessl-carnival` to it.

A workspace is the folder Tessl uses for this account: the factory, its automations, and the credit balance live there. This new account has 11,000 credits and no workspace yet. Setup does not create that workspace for you.

**What this repo is making me do.** You asked me to follow `workshop/agent.md` one step at a time. That guide, plus `AGENTS.md`, is the constraint. The repository does not block edits. Nothing in the code refuses a change.

The path you set is:

2. Set up a Tessl factory on your fork. That is the step we are in. It needs a workspace, then two GitHub app installs in the browser, then a yes before anything is turned on, because the fork is public.
3. After the factory is live, a change becomes a GitHub issue with a **Done when** checklist. Adding the `tessl` label starts a cloud agent. That agent writes the code and opens a pull request. I am not supposed to write the game or open the pull request myself. You merge it, and GitHub Pages redeploys.

For a game, the issue also has to follow the carnival’s house rules: its own folder under `src/games/`, scores only through the shared scores module, colors and fonts only from the shared theme, and game logic tested without a browser. A new game fills the next Coming soon booth on its own. The map does not need a separate edit.
